episode: 2023 Yeezy loss and inventory clean-up (Gulden from Jan 2023)
actions: Conservative wholesale sell-in, North America deliberately shrunk 7 quarters, sold Yeezy stock instead of writing it off, scaled Terrace supply below demand
quarters_to_gm_recovery: 2 quarters to first y/y gain (Yeezy-aided, Q2 2023); 4 to 5 quarters to clean gain (Q4 2023 +5.5pp, Q1 2024 +6.4pp)
price_metric: Not disclosed as ASP; 2024 gains "driven by lower product and freight costs" plus less discounting
revenue_given_up: About EUR 1.2B Yeezy revenue (2022 level); North America -16% c.n. in 2023; 2023 group c.n. 0%
outcome: Recovered and exceeded pre-crisis GM within 2 years; revenue +12% c.n. 2024
source: research_notes/Gulden and Plank turnarounds vs Nike/adidas_gulden.md (adidas FY2022-Q2 2026 releases)

actions: Cleared inventory through off-price in 2018, then cut off-price share of wholesale from 2019; in 2021 "exiting undifferentiated retail"
quarters_to_gm_recovery: About 4 to 5 quarters from inventory peak to first annual GM gain (FY2019; annual data only); 2015 level regained in 2020 (3 years)
price_metric: Channel mix from less off-price: about +50 bps (2019) and about +220 bps (2020)
revenue_given_up: North America -$76.9M (-2%) in 2019 "due to a unit sales decrease of off-price sales"; total 2019 +1%
outcome: GM up 520 bps 2018 to 2021; revenue flat 2017 to 2019

actions: Planned promotional cuts (eCommerce -20% to -27% a quarter in FY2025), about 25% fewer SKUs, tighter distribution, restructuring up to about $305M

episode: FY2017 to FY2019 Way Forward Plan
actions: Strategic reduction of wholesale shipments including off-price; closed about 25% of underperforming U.S. department store doors in FY2018; lower promotional activity
gm_path: FY2016 56.5%; FY2017 54.9% (57.9% ex $197.9M inventory charges, my arithmetic); FY2018 60.7% (adj +290 bps); FY2019 61.6% (adj +90 bps); FY2020 59.3% (COVID charges); FY2026 69.9% (XBRL, my arithmetic)
quarters_to_gm_recovery: Adjusted GM up in every quarter of FY2018, i.e. 4 to 7 quarters after the Apr 2016 inventory peak; underlying GM already up in FY2017
price_metric: DTC AUR +4% FY2018 ("growth in every quarter"), +8% FY2019, +3% FY2020 (+8% Q4 FY2020)
revenue_given_up: $7,405M FY2016 to $6,182M FY2018 (-16.5%, my arithmetic); North America -15.6% FY2017 and -14.6% FY2018; FY2015 revenue peak ($7,620M) regained only in FY2026
outcome: Success on margin and AUR within 2 years; revenue took about 3 years to grow again and a decade to pass its old peak
